f-P17j: Create a no-secrets rule. No grownup has a right to ask a kid to keep a secret from their mom or another trusted adult, whether it's about a gift, a game, a touch, a conversation or a relationship. A surprise isn't a secret, because at the end of a certain date it has to be told. But secrets meant to isolate a kid aren't allowed.

f-P18j: Teach truthfulness before there's a crisis. Talk with the kids about the importance of telling the truth, the power of their words, and how what they say will be taken seriously. Don't let the teaching turn into interrogation, punishment when they're not sure, or a reason to brush off what they report. A scared or confused kid may tell it badly and still need protection.
f-P25b5: Kids also need a good set of transferable skills and education, good relationships with people outside the community, access to their own records and documents, and at least one plausible next step outside the community (school, an apprenticeship, work, family, another community). It would be great if the community could also provide resources to smooth the transition, like temporary housing, travel expenses, tools or a little money, but even if it can't, it can at least not make things worse by punishing people for leaving, or by holding back knowledge or records a young adult would need to function outside the community. No upbringing can provide perfect freedom, and the point isn't to erase path dependence. It's to not turn belonging into a trap.
